entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Marcus Argentarius was a Greek epigrammatist who flourished in the 3rd century BC.

Born in Smyrna, Asia Minor (modern-day İzmir, Turkey), Argentarius is best known for his collection of epigrams, 'Argenta' (Αεηβλτα).

His epigrams are notable for their wit and clever wordplay, often incorporating puns and double meanings.

Argentarius' work had a significant impact on the development of Greek poetry, influencing later poets such as Ovid and Martial.

He is also remembered for his contributions to the literary magazine 'Philogelos', which featured humorous writings and anecdotes.

Despite his significance in the world of ancient Greek literature, little is known about Argentarius' personal life or the circumstances of his death.

Argentarius' legacy as a master of witty epigrams continues to be celebrated by scholars and readers alike.

One striking statistic about Argentarius is that his collection of 300 epigrams remains one of the most extensive and diverse in ancient Greek literature.
